title: Intervention modules to promote self-management of geriatric syndromes: A feasibility study
summary:
Self-management means that patients do something for their health, for example taking their medication, eating healthily and undergoing therapy. Self-management also includes psychosocial aspects such as dealing with emotions, making decisions and maintaining social contacts. Programs that support people in taking care of their own health have the potential to improve health. They can also improve quality of life and reduce costs in the healthcare system. Older people have a higher risk of illness. They often have several chronic diseases. However, existing programs often only address individual diseases, such as diabetes or osteoarthritis.
We have developed several modules that focus on self-management of overarching geriatric syndromes, rather than individual diseases. Geriatric syndromes are problems that affect many older people. These include falls and restricted mobility. We now want to test the feasibility and acceptance of the developed modules. This preliminary study should help to further improve the modules and to develop a future study to test the effectiveness of the modules.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Geriatric patients admitted to an acute geriatric ward
•	Sufficient mobility to reach the room designated for the intervention independently or with use of mobility aids, as assessed by ward staff
•	Barthel Index ≥ 40
•	Subjectively capable of participating in the intervention and understanding instructions, according to the clinical assessment of the treating physicians and research staff
•	Expected to be available by telephone after hospitalization
•	Consent to audio recording of interviews
•	Receives at least one module according to the decision algorithm
Exclusion criteria:
•	Documented diagnosis of dementia
•	Acute delirium or psychosis
•	Acute suicidality
•	Barthel Index < 40
•	Diagnosis of a disease that impairs the capacity to consent to participation 
•	Unlikely to be available by telephone after discharge
•	No consent to audio recording of interviews
